Reading and writing notes are not here: they never ask, because trash and version history put every one of them back — and a log with them in it would bury the entries that matter. None of this syncs; allowing something here is not allowing it on another device.
syn.permissions_none: Nothing has been asked for yet.

syn.footing_guessing_why: Nothing held this up — no tool call, no retrieved text, no count, and nothing read from the web. Check it before acting on it.

syn.stats_private: Counted on this device from files in your Synabit folder. These numbers are never sent anywhere.
syn.stats_empty: No runs in this period yet. Ask Syn something and come back.
syn.stats_on_disk_note: The last {kept} runs are kept, so this goes back to {since}.
syn.stats_measured: Measured on {n} of {total} runs. Runs from before this was recorded are left out, not counted as zero.
syn.stats_not_measured: Not measured yet — runs from before this was recorded are not counted.
syn.stats_runs_total_why: Every question Syn worked on — what everything below is out of.
syn.stats_surface_why: Where questions came from. A place at zero is one nobody is using.
syn.stats_rounds_why: Each round sends the whole conversation again, so rounds are what a run costs. Many runs past ten means Syn is searching instead of answering.
syn.stats_asked: Stopped to ask {asked} times — {per100} per 100 runs. {carried} were answered and carried on, so they are not counted as endings above.
syn.stats_ended_why: Anything but done is worth a look. Many runs cut short means the limits are too tight or Syn is going round in circles.
syn.stats_ceiling_title: Which limit cut a run short
syn.stats_ceiling_why: The target is under 10% of all runs. If “Could not tell” starts growing, the note Syn leaves when it stops has changed wording and this count needs fixing.
syn.stats_ceiling_none: No run was cut short by a limit.
syn.stats_tools_why: Each of these was built on a bet that the model would reach for it. Zero after two weeks means the bet lost.
syn.stats_tool_load_skill: Skills Syn chose to open. If this is 0 after two weeks, skills are not being used.
syn.stats_tool_run_recipe: Recipes run from start to finish. Zero means recipe skills exist only on paper.
syn.stats_tool_remember: Things Syn decided to remember. Zero means memory only grows when you add to it yourself.
syn.stats_tool_recall: Searches of what Syn remembers. It once went unused for weeks; this is how you would notice again.
syn.stats_tool_look_back: Reads of earlier conversations. Zero means Syn never uses its own history.
syn.stats_tool_browse: Web pages read. Worth knowing before worrying about what the web can do to a run.
syn.stats_tool_update_plan: Step lists written or updated. Zero means long runs never show you a plan.
syn.stats_memory_share: Runs with memory in the prompt
syn.stats_memory_share_why: Memory only helps if it reaches the model. Counted from the prompt as it was sent.
syn.stats_memory_avg: Memory lines, per run that had any
syn.stats_memory_dropped: Memory lines left out for room
syn.stats_memory_dropped_why: Things you told Syn that it was not shown. The target is under 10%.
syn.stats_prompt_dropped: Runs where a whole part of the prompt was cut to fit
syn.stats_prompt_dropped_why: Cut to stay inside the model’s window. Retrieved notes go first, memory last.
syn.stats_skills_offered: Runs where skills were on offer
syn.stats_skills_offered_why: Runs whose prompt listed at least one skill — what skill loads should be compared against.
syn.stats_skills_loaded_why: A skill that is switched on and never opened is doing nothing.
syn.stats_retrieval_value: {avg} ms on average, {max} ms at the slowest
syn.stats_retrieval_why: The wait before the first word that you cannot see happening. Not measured when retrieval is switched off.
syn.stats_footing_why: Whether an answer was looked up, read around, or held up by nothing from your notes.
syn.stats_tokens_why: Tokens charged, sent and written, every round counted. Cached is the part the provider served from its cache, which costs less.
syn.stats_tokens_total: {tokens} tokens for the runs above, {cached} of them cached.

syn.tools_undo_nothing: Nothing to undo — it only reads.

syn.tools_group_cost: {chars} characters of every turn, about {tokens} tokens

syn.tier_hosted_says: This model runs elsewhere. Each question, and the notes, tool results and memories Syn reads to answer it, are sent to it.
syn.tier_reasoning: Thinks before answering, and is billed for it
syn.tier_guessed: This model is not one Syn knows by name, so these are careful guesses.
syn.doing_delegate: Handing part of the work to a helper
syn.connector_intro: Connect Syn to the world outside your notes — an issue tracker, a database, a program on this computer — and it can use their tools. Every read through a connector asks once; everything that sends asks for that tool.
syn.connector_honest: Tools on this connector see what Syn sends them; results are treated as untrusted.
syn.connector_url_hint: Saved in your Synabit folder, which syncs. Put a key or token in a secret header below, never in the address.

syn.connector_test_none: It answers, and offers no tools.
syn.connector_remove_confirm: Remove {name}? Its secrets on this device and every permission given to it go too.
syn.connector_status_desktop_only: This connector needs the desktop app.
syn.connector_status_not_trusted_here: Added or changed on another device. Open it and save it here to connect on this one.
syn.routines_explainer: Questions Syn asks itself at a time you choose. A routine can read and look things up and write a new note; it cannot change or remove anything. What it finds goes to its own conversation, Syn's work and, if you like, your phone. Only you can create one.

syn.doing_safe_health: Looking at how healthy your passwords are

safe.name: Safe

intro.title: Safe
intro.body: A place for your passwords, keys and codes. Only you can open it — not Synabit, not Syn.
points: Everything is encrypted on this device before it is written.
Opening it takes your master password and a Secret Key only this device holds.
Syn never sees a value. Later, you can let it use one without seeing it.
intro.other_device: Already have a Safe on another device? Don't make a new one here — let sync bring it, and this screen asks for its password by itself.

setup.password_body: The one password you will need to remember. Long beats clever.
setup.warning: If you forget this password and lose your Emergency Kit, your Safe cannot be opened. Nobody can recover it — including us.
setup.creating_hint: Tuning the encryption to this device. This takes a few seconds.

kit.title: Your Secret Key
kit.body: Write these twelve words down, or save the Emergency Kit and print it. With your master password, they open this Safe on any device.
kit.not_stored: This device's keychain refused the Secret Key. You will need to type these words each time you unlock.
kit.confirm: I have written these words down or saved the kit somewhere safe

unlock.changed_elsewhere: If you changed the master password or the Secret Key on another device, use the new one here. If you did not, the Safe can go back to the password you have been using — it then replaces the other device's change everywhere.
unlock.use_previous: I did not change it — use my password
unlock.forgot_body: It cannot be reset or recovered. Synabit never stores it, so nobody — not us, not Syn — can look it up or send you a new one.
unlock.forgot_kit: If you wrote it in the box on your printed Emergency Kit, look there. The twelve words on the kit do not replace it: they open the Safe only together with the master password. Without it, what is in this Safe stays locked.
